newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia mineral export income steady - ABARE.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia mineral export income steady - ABARE.

text.p: Export earnings by Australia's minerals and energy sector were up 0.7 percent at A$8.55 billion in the December quarter compared with a year earlier, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics said.

The strong performance reflected increased export earnings across a wide range of commodities, with petroleum refinery products, coal, crude oil and copper most notable, Brian Fisher, ABARE's executive director, said in a statement ahead of the March 18 release of latest Australian Commodities forecasts.

Export earnings for petroleum refinery products rose 47 percent to A$359 million; steaming coal rose 12 percent to A$807 million; crude oil and other refinery feedstock rose 13 percent to A$519 million and copper rose 23 percent to A$272 million.

Smaller rises were recorded for alumina, up 5.3 percent to A$653 million; coking coal, up 2.9 percent to A$1.19 billion; liquefied natural gas, up 9.4 percent to A$383 million; and uranium, up 66 percent to A$63 million.
Increased export volumes were the main reason for the increase in export values, Fisher said.
For crude oil, gas and petroleum refinery products, however, higher world prices also contributed.

Minerals showing significant falls in export earnings during the December quarter were: refined gold, down 9.5 percent to A$1.24 billion; aluminium down 21 percent to A$426 million; diamonds, down 15 percent to A$142 million; iron ore, down 3.1 percent to A$743 million; nickel, down 5.8 percent to A$259 million; iron, steel and ferro-alloys, down 4.1 percent to A$375 million; and zinc, down 7.3 percent to A$191 million.
Both lower export volumes and world prices contributed to the falls, Fisher said.
The index of export prices of Australian mineral resources fell marginally in the December quarter compared with the September quarter of 1996.
An increase of 3.2 percent in the energy minerals component was offset by a 2.4 percent decline in the metals and other minerals component.
